Dashcam Video of Violent Arrest of Sandra Bland Was Edited

Are there any reasons why the police would release edited footage? Is it possible that the camera cut out or something? I don't think it's helpful to jump to conclusions as to *why *the video was edited but it does seem questionable.

Eh, I finally actually watched the whole thing and now I lean more towards it just being glitches somewhere in the recording/converting/uploading process. (The audio ends 3 minutes before the video does, which makes sense with the crazy looping shit going on in parts of the video.)

I don't know. To me it looks like they just snipped the timeline and shuffled the same start point at various instances down the project timeline. If it were a glitch, the jump cuts wouldn't be so clean and precise. The video would pixelize or de-res for a frame or two if it were an actual corruption via the process of recording/uploading. There are two small instances repeated in the loop of an instance of that, but they're part of the raw footage- those were legit corruptions in the process. They wouldn't keep showing up in the same spot, it would be all over the frame throughout, but it's not. They're at the same point in the frame at the same times in relation to the cars on the road.

This thing just reeks of BS.

EDIT: Wanted to add that if it was a corruption in the capture process, the audio wouldn't be as smooth as it is during that whole sequence. It too would be a garbled mess much like the video.
I don't think the audio ends so much as it was disabled. There's a sort of shutting down type bleep sound played right before the audio track ends.

Well, since the video track has been edited there's no way to validate the authenticity of the audio track either. Any amount of time on that phone call where these edits took place could have been removed from that audio track and replaced with background noise.

The only thing in my mind is that he said something incriminating on that phone-call while in the car. He clearly doesn't remember the whole incident, or at least isn't reporting it as the video captured it, to whomever is on the other end. He made no mention of the cigarette or threatening to "light her up" on that phone call, or... maybe he did and it was edited out.

With the FBI involved though, as I've stated in another thread elsewhere, I'm just simply stumped that this mockery would be released to the public. Then again, with the FBI now involved, maybe I shouldn't be so surprised edited video is being released.

• At 23:24 he enters his vehicle and you can see the video is perfectly in sync as you can see his vehicle shake slightly as he sits down.

  • At 35:57 you can hear him enter or leave his vehicle again, yet the camera doesn't shake in the least.

So by 35:57 the video and audio were out of synch. Numerous times during the video you can hear the Windows error or invalid action alert sound being played such as, among others, at 30:21. I'm going to assume that their audio/video setup is software controlled which means those alerts may have been related. Also the main reason you'd maliciously loop video is to synch the audio, yet the audio and video remained out of synch. Towards the later part of the video there was plenty of down time with nothing happening and no way to link the audio to outside events meaning they could have added audio without even editing the video. And somebody maliciously editing things in likely would have the knowledge to at least ensure there were no large gaping and obvious loops. Consequently I don't think this is malicious. It just looks like their software was bugging out.
I'm having a hard time buying the "it's a bug". I would expect to see a lot more pixelation and 'digital mess' and not such crisp edits.

Start making job hunting your job.

First thing. Watch your social media use. Don't bitch about the place that fired you and get rid of any extreme party type posts. From this point til you're hired you are white bread america according to facebook. Also as of right now it seems like there's all sorts of openings that fit your skills, but trust me you'll run out of those quickly and a month or 2 months or like me 8 months from now new ads that fit you will be a trickle. Sure you can shoot out applications and resumes out like a machine gun, but like a machine gun you're pretty much hoping for just 1 out of 20 shots to land and once those bullets are fired they're gone forever. You've gotta be a sniper and conserve every shot you take and put it best on target as you can.

Honestly you should spend at least an hour on each resume you send out. Research the company and tailor your resume and cover letter to fit that company specifically being sure to use whatever buzzwords seemed important to them in their job posting. Oh yeah, switch over to a professional voice mail non robotic greeting right now. Hell this paragraph isn't enough, go do some research on writing resumes and cover letters.

And if you feel you're not quite qualified for a position do it all on a lark. Some companies still let applicants know that they were rejected for whatever reason. Make it your goal to get at least five of those messages before your search is over.

Keep downtime to a minimum, that is the quickest way to start getting the hopeless feelings that will eat at you and make you less productive. Stay vigilant and send out apps/resumes like they pay you to do them, flood the market with you. Apply for any job you think you may not qualify for but that isnt a huge gap (if you have a AAS don't apply for a PhD job but definitely apply for BS jobs). Check with local staffers for temp work to get you by, and don't be afraid to take a "lowly" job you think is beneath you to make ends meet in the mean time. Too many people end up unemployed and get the mentality of "I am too good to work fast food" and thats bullshit, if you don't have a job any job is a step in the right direction.
